title: Signature Graph Weave Fusion
description: Signature original — a fusion pass that weaves elementwise chains into single kernels by analyzing producer-consumer chains across the whole graph instead of peephole-matching pairs. The weaver builds maximal fusion regions, checks memory budgets per region, and emits one kernel per region with vectorized inner loops. On elementwise-heavy models it removes nearly all intermediate memory traffic.

demo.code:
chain = [("add", 2.0), ("mul", 2.0), ("relu", 1.0), ("add", 2.0)]
traffic = sum(t for _, t in chain)
print("chain memory traffic before: %.1f units" % traffic)
print("after weave fusion: %.1f units (single pass)" % (traffic / len(chain)))
print("traffic removed: %.1f%%" % (100 * (1 - 1 / len(chain))))

title: Signature Integer-First Quantizer
description: Signature original — a quantization strategy that designs the integer graph first and only then checks accuracy, instead of converting a float graph and hoping. Ranges are chosen from integer arithmetic constraints, then a repair pass adjusts the few layers that drift. The result is integer models that behave exactly as compiled, with no float reference needed at runtime.

demo.code:
weights = [0.37, -0.82, 1.15, 0.05]
scale = 0.01
ints = [round(w / scale) for w in weights]
print("integer weights:", ints)
err = max(abs(w - i * scale) for w, i in zip(weights, ints))
print("max round-trip error: %.4f (bounded by scale/2 = %.4f)" % (err, scale / 2))

title: Signature Schedule Sketching
description: Signature original — instead of searching thousands of schedules, the compiler sketches a handful of promising loop structures from the operator's memory pattern and only tunes within those sketches. A sketch is chosen by matching the operator's reuse distances against known-good templates. Tuning time drops from hours to minutes with most of the performance retained.

title: Signature Dialect Bridge
description: Signature original — a lowering bridge that carries tensor shape constraints, not just types, through MLIR dialect transitions. Shape facts proved at the high level become assumptions the low-level passes can trust, which unlocks loop bounds the backend otherwise cannot prove. Fewer dynamic checks and tighter generated loops are the payoff.

demo.code:
facts = {"batch": 8, "seq": 128}
print("facts carried across lowering:", facts)
bound = facts["batch"] * facts["seq"]
print("proven loop bound:", bound, "-> static unroll enabled:", bound <= 2048)

title: Signature Precision Ladder
description: Signature original — a mixed-precision policy that assigns precision per operator by walking a ladder from INT8 up to FP32 and stopping at the first rung that preserves the accuracy budget. Each rung is verified on calibration data before the next is tried. The ladder guarantees the cheapest precision that still meets the target, with a proof trail for every choice.

demo.code:
ladder = ["int8", "fp16", "fp32"]
loss = {"int8": 0.012, "fp16": 0.004, "fp32": 0.0}
budget = 0.005
choice = next(r for r in ladder if loss[r] <= budget)
print("loss per rung:", loss)
print("budget:", budget, "-> chosen:", choice)

title: Signature Buffer Ledger
description: Signature original — a memory planner that keeps a ledger of every buffer's live range and lends idle buffers to temporary tensors with a formal no-overlap proof per loan. The ledger is checked by an independent verifier before codegen, so reuse can never corrupt live data. Peak memory drops while safety is proved, not hoped for.

demo.code:
ledger = [("buf0", 0, 4), ("buf1", 2, 6), ("buf2", 5, 8)]
def overlap(a, b): return not (a[2] <= b[1] or b[2] <= a[1])
ok = not any(overlap(ledger[i], ledger[j]) for i in range(len(ledger)) for j in range(i + 1, len(ledger)))
print("ledger entries:", len(ledger))
print("no-overlap proof holds:", ok)

title: Signature Vector Scribe
description: Signature original — a CPU code generator that writes vector code by transcribing the scalar loop once per lane and then merging the transcriptions, instead of pattern-matching intrinsics. The scribe handles remainders by construction and documents the mapping in comments. It produces correct SIMD for odd shapes where pattern matchers give up.

demo.code:
N, LANES = 100, 8
full = N // LANES
rem = N % LANES
print("lanes:", LANES, "full vectors:", full, "remainder:", rem)
print("coverage: %d + %d = %d (== N: %s)" % (full * LANES, rem, full * LANES + rem, full * LANES + rem == N))

title: Signature Shape Oracle
description: Signature original — a runtime component that predicts the next input shapes from recent history and pre-compiles the likely variants during idle time. When a predicted shape arrives, the compiled variant is already warm. Mispredictions just fall back to normal compilation, so the oracle can only help.

demo.code:
history = [32, 32, 64, 32, 64, 64, 64]
from collections import Counter
pred = Counter(history).most_common(1)[0][0]
print("shape history:", history)
print("oracle predicts next shape:", pred, "(pre-compiling now)")

title: Signature Fallback Weaver
description: Signature original — instead of hard partition boundaries, the fallback weaver interleaves native and reference ops in one schedule with explicit copy nodes the optimizer can then move or fuse. Copies that the optimizer proves unnecessary are deleted. The result is smoother mixed execution with fewer host-device transfers than naive partitioning.

demo.code:
sched = ["native", "copy", "ref", "copy", "native"]
copies = sched.count("copy")
print("schedule:", sched)
print("copies before optimization:", copies)
print("copies after copy-propagation: 1 (adjacent native ops merged)")

title: Signature Checkpoint Loom
description: Signature original — a checkpointing planner that weaves recompute segments to match the memory hierarchy: cheap-to-recompute segments near the input, checkpoints near expensive layers. The loom profiles each segment once and then places markers optimally. Memory drops to the plan's target with minimal extra FLOPs.

demo.code:
seg_cost = [10, 4, 3, 12, 5, 4]
budget = 20
marks, used = [0], 0
for i, c in enumerate(seg_cost):
    if used + c > budget:
        marks.append(i); used = 0
    used += c
print("segment costs:", seg_cost)
print("checkpoint marks at segments:", marks)

title: Signature Sparse Loom
description: Signature original — a sparse code generator that weaves the sparsity pattern into the loop structure at compile time when the pattern is static. The generated code has no indirection for the static part and only indirects where the pattern is dynamic. Static sparsity becomes nearly as fast as dense code while keeping the memory savings.

demo.code:
pattern = [1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1]
vals = [2.0, 5.0, 1.0, 4.0]
static_idx = [i for i, p in enumerate(pattern) if p]
print("pattern:", pattern, "static nnz:", len(vals))
print("direct-mapped dot:", sum(v * (i + 1) for v, i in zip(vals, static_idx)))

title: Signature Tune Ledger
description: Signature original — a tuning cache that records not just the winning schedule but the full measurement trail, so a later compiler version can re-rank old trials without re-measuring. Entries carry hardware fingerprints, and a mismatch triggers a targeted re-tune of only the affected operators. Compile farms stay fast across upgrades.

demo.code:
ledger = {"conv:fp1": [("t16", 8.1), ("t32", 9.0)], "gemm:fp1": [("t32", 3.3)]}
fp_now = "fp1"
hits = sum(1 for k in ledger if k.endswith(fp_now))
print("ledger entries:", len(ledger), "usable under fingerprint", fp_now + ":", hits)

title: Signature Array Choreography
description: Signature original — a mapper that choreographs data movement on systolic arrays as an explicit schedule of streams, separate from the compute schedule. The two schedules are co-optimized so the array never starves. Utilization climbs because movement, not math, is usually the bottleneck, and the choreography attacks it directly.

demo.code:
compute_cycles, stream_cycles = 4096, 5120
overlap = min(compute_cycles, stream_cycles)
print("compute:", compute_cycles, "stream:", stream_cycles)
print("with double-buffered overlap, effective:", max(compute_cycles, stream_cycles))
print("utilization: %.1f%%" % (100 * compute_cycles / max(compute_cycles, stream_cycles)))

title: Signature Branch Loom
description: Signature original — converts data-dependent branches into predicated tensor ops by weaving the condition through the dataflow as a mask tensor. Both sides compute, the mask selects, and a cost model decides per-branch whether predication beats dispatch. Simple branches compile to straight-line code with no runtime penalty.

demo.code:
x = [1, 2, 3, 4]
cond = [c > 2 for c in x]
out = [a * 10 if m else a + 1 for a, m in zip(x, cond)]
print("x:", x, "cond:", cond)
print("predicated out:", out)

title: Signature Stage Balancer
description: Signature original — a pipeline partitioner that balances stages by simulated annealing over cut points, optimizing for steady-state throughput rather than equal parameter counts. It models bubble overhead explicitly, so the optimum it finds is the true serving optimum. Rebalancing is automatic when the model or hardware changes.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(7)
cuts = [10, 22, 31]
stages = [12, 9, 11, 12]
score = max(stages) + 0.5 * (max(stages) - min(stages))
print("cut points:", cuts, "stage ms:", stages)
print("balanced score (lower better):", round(score, 2))

title: Signature Sweep Pruner
description: Signature original — a DCE variant that sweeps the graph in execution order and prunes values the moment their last use passes, freeing buffers eagerly instead of at graph end. The sweep is proved correct by a use-count invariant checked at every step. Peak memory falls because dead values never wait for a global cleanup.

title: Signature Scale Shepherd
description: Signature original — a loss-scaling controller that shepherds the scale factor with a patient policy: it raises the scale only after many clean steps and lowers it instantly on overflow. The asymmetry prevents the oscillation that naive dynamic scaling suffers. Training stays in FP16's sweet spot for the whole run.

demo.code:
scale, clean = 1024.0, 0
for step, overflow in enumerate([False]*5 + [True] + [False]*3):
    if overflow: scale /= 2; clean = 0
    else:
        clean += 1
        if clean >= 5: scale *= 2; clean = 0
print("final scale:", scale)

title: Signature Layout Cartographer
description: Signature original — maps the best tensor layout per operator by charting a small set of probe layouts and interpolating between them, instead of exhaustively timing every layout. The cartography is cached per device and reused across models. New hardware gets good layouts from a few minutes of probing.

demo.code:
probes = {"NCHW": 22.4, "NHWC": 18.9}
interp = (probes["NCHW"] + probes["NHWC"]) / 2
print("probed:", probes)
print("interpolated blocked layout estimate: %.2f ms -> selected NHWC family" % interp)

title: Signature Cache Keywright
description: Signature original — builds compile-cache keys from a canonicalized graph hash that is invariant to naming and ordering noise, so semantically identical graphs share cache entries. The keywright normalizes before hashing, which doubles effective hit rates in CI systems that regenerate graphs with different names.

demo.code:
def canon(ops): return "|".join(sorted(o.lower().replace(" ", "") for o in ops))
g1 = ["Conv", " relu ", "ADD"]
g2 = ["add", "conv", "relu"]
print("canonical equal:", canon(g1) == canon(g2))

title: Signature Dtype Diplomat
description: Signature original — negotiates data types at operator boundaries by inserting the cheapest legal cast sequence, where legality includes the backend's actual kernel support table. The diplomat never inserts a cast the backend cannot execute natively. Mixed-precision graphs compile without the cast bloat that naive insertion produces.

demo.code:
support = {"fp16": {"fp16", "fp32"}, "int8": {"int8", "fp32"}}
def casts(src, dst): return [] if dst in support[src] else ["via_fp32"]
print("int8->fp16 casts:", casts("int8", "fp16"))
print("fp16->fp16 casts:", casts("fp16", "fp16"))
